items.text: Haha, Starešina Krčme, Stari – odlično. Zadel si, Leopard Farid.
items.q: Hooman shortens the nickname 'Starešina Krčme' to a pet form. Does 'Stari' work as that short nickname?
before: Hooman je s pisalom pisal kaj v knjigo in rekel:

items.text: Krčmar je, po resnici in pravici povedano.
items.q: Farid adds a third nickname for Amir, 'Krčmar', from the same tavern idea. Does it sound natural as a nickname?
before: Hooman je s pisalom pisal kaj v knjigo in rekel:
– Haha, Starešina Krčme, Stari – odlično. Zadel si, Leopard Farid.

items.text: Dež ne pada navzgor iz zemlje. Tudi stari so imeli dobre reke.
items.q: Maman quotes an old saying and says the old folks had good sayings. Does 'dobre reke' mean good sayings here?
before: – Bog ne daj, ne govori tako. Ni otrok tisti, ki naj bo žrtev — ampak mati.

items.text: Potakni nos v vsak košček. Stari so vedno govorili: pokukaj v vsak zadnji kotiček.
items.q: Maman urges her son to explore and quotes an old saying. Does it sound like a folk saying she would use?
before: – Mm-hm, prav delaš. Dokler imaš priložnost, pojdi in si oglej vse vasi.

items.text: Tako pač govorim. Vi mislite, da recitujem pesmi.
items.q: Hamid, a boy, answers in the rhythm and rhyme of his own poems. Does this line sound like a playful rhyme?
before: Hamid je rekel v istem ritmu, s katerim je recitiral svoje pesmi:

items.text: Huh. Prijatelj bratranca mojstra našega svaka, ki je najbogatejši človek v Teheranu, govori natanko tako.
items.q: Hamid, a boy, always boasts about a long chain of contacts ending in a rich man. Does this running joke sound natural and funny?

items.text: Najprej pridite in dokumentirajte ta palec, potem pa snemajte film o čemerkoli hočete.
items.q: Hooman sticks up his thumb, a rude gesture in Iran, to mock Farid's film idea. Does this read as a rude joke?
before: – Fantje, dajmo posneti dokumentarni film o naši sobi.
Hooman je izvlekel roko izpod odeje in rekel:

items.text: Naj krožim okoli tebe, jigaram. Vedno se smej.
items.q: Maman tells her son she would circle around him again and again, an old loving phrase. Does this line sound tender?
before: Nasmehnem se in poizkušam raztegniti kožo na čelu, kolikor le zmorem.

items.text: Bilo je pozno, ko sem prišel v dijaški dom.
items.q: Amir, a university student, comes back late to the dormitory where he lives. Does 'dijaški dom' fit here?

items.text: V istem hipu je ščurek privleklo izpod Hoomanovei postelje in se vrnil pod njo.
items.q: A cockroach runs out from under Hooman's bed and back again. Does this sentence read correctly?

items.text: Ko se naša imena navad, ji bomo všeč.
items.q: A boy spray-painting their names says the girl will like them once she learns the names. Does this line read correctly?
before: Yaser je s sprejem, ki ga je suknil iz očetovega tovornjaka, na zid nasproti Negarine hiše pisal naša imena in govoril:

items.text: Zaobljubla sem se, da bom, če mu bo bolje, peš romala v Mašhad.
items.q: Maman made a religious vow to walk to the shrine city if her son recovers. Does this line read correctly?
before: …ki je sedel v dnevni sobi pred televizorjem in luščil bučna semena, in Maman, ki je sedela ob njem. Poročila so govorila o škodi zaradi obsežnih poplav v severnih in zahodnih provincah dežele. Od zadaj se mi je Maman zazdela kakor majhen krog, ki sedi ob večjem pravokotniku. Maman je govorila:

items.text: Torej namesto dežja pada s neba prst.
items.q: A girl leads a playful imagination game: earth falls from the sky instead of rain. Does this sentence read correctly?
before: – Zdaj si zamišljaj, da sva na planetu sredi druge galaksije. Tu je zemlja iz vode in nebo iz prsti.

items.text: Godrnjanje? Godrnjanje je, kadar ti niso storili nič slabega.
items.q: Maman, irritated, says talking about someone only counts as gossip if they haven't wronged you. Does 'Godrnjanje' mean gossip here?
before: Maman obrne glavo v smer Mahboubehinega glasu in z rahlo razdraženim tonom reče:

items.text: Huh, poglejte – se kateremu od vas spomni ena dobra stvar pri vašem Babi?
items.q: Maman challenges her children to name one good thing about their father. Does this question read correctly?

items.text: Ja. Tega Arasteja ne glej; pa naj je še tako čvekast, rang na Konkoorju mu je bil štiriinsedemdeset.
items.q: Hooman calls quiet, dreamy Amir goofy but brags about his top exam rank. Does 'čvekast' fit for goofy?
